Thanks for the ping — I reviewed the redlines and attached a redlined DPA with in-line comments (redlined_DPA_LB_20261111.docx). High-level position: we can close this quickly with a few commercial concessions. My notes below.

Summary of legal positions (short):
- Role: Redwood confirms it will act as Processor for customer data under the MSA. We will not accept Joint Controller status for the standard integrations described. Please ensure the Order Form does not expand controller obligations.
- SCCs: We can adopt the EU SCCs as the transfer mechanism; Redwood will sign the SCC Controller-to-Processor Annex where required. We cannot provide a standalone transfer impact assessment always — we will supply a summary of technical/organizational measures and any subsidiary TIA on request.
- Subprocessors: We propose the standard 30-day notice; our objection window is 14 days. If NimbleHealth objects, we'll provide a remediation plan and, only in narrow circumstances, negotiate substitution.
- Audit rights: limit to annual audits with notice and scope to avoid broad operational disruption. Prefer to accept third-party SOC2 reports in lieu of intrusive onsite audits.
- Security measures: reference Annex A (we will provide the latest security controls matrix); do not enumerate highly sensitive proprietary protections in the DPA text.
- Liability/indemnity: we will align data processing liability to the caps in the underlying MSA/Order Form; we cannot accept uncapped exposure on infrastructure outages not caused by Redwood negligence.

Open items for commercial team:
1) Data retention term in the Order Form — NimbleHealth has a specific retention period; confirm whether we map to that or ask for minimal retention necessary.
2) SLA carveouts for DPA obligations — confirm desired escalation paths.

Requested timeline: please confirm if NimbleHealth can accept Processor role and the SCC route by 11/12 EOD. If yes, we'll produce the redlined DPA and a one-page transfer summary for execution.

Regards,
